thread:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a perf regression on prod after we enabled the shape-aware autotuner + torch.compile path for the new LlamaX model. p99 gen latency jumped ~18% on short conversations (<=64 tokens).
kevin: Ugh. Can you paste the profile?
maria: Quick summary from the tracing run (devbox, A100):
```
- baseline (no compile, dynamic kernels): p50 38ms, p99 120ms
- autotuner + torch.compile (capture): p50 34ms, p99 142ms
- autotuner + no-compile (forcing uncaptured): p50 36ms, p99 118ms
Notes: delta mainly in p99, throughput steady. KV cache hit-rate unchanged.
```
oliver: Interesting — looks like capture + autotuner picks a different kernel for the small seqlen bucket, probably optimizing for long sequences and regressing short tail. Did you get kernel selection logs?
maria: Yes, here's a snip from the kernel picker in the trace:
```
SEQLEN_BUCKET=short (<=64) -> chosen_kernel=matmul_fused_v2_f32 (score 78)
with compile/capture -> chosen_kernel=matmul_fused_v1_int8 (score 81)
reason: capture prefers a smaller kernel set that matches captured ops
```
anna: That matches my local: torch.compile seems to cause graph normalization so the autotuner sees a different op pattern (fewer variants), it collapses certain dynamic dispatches. The tuning objective function then favors a slightly different micro-kernel that is worse for short sequences.
kevin: Any quick mitigations? Can we force kernel family for short sequences while still keeping compile for long ones?
maria: Tried a hotfix: if seq_len <= 128, disable compile and fall back to uncaptured runtime — restores p99 to baseline. Patch diff (toy):
```
if seq_len <= 128 and env.DISABLE_COMPILE_SHORT == "1":
    executor = runtime_executor
else:
    executor = compiled_executor
```
oliver: That's pragmatic. But we need automated detection — maybe warmup/capture should include representative short traces so capture doesn't over-constrain kernels. Could also add an autotune pass that runs microbenchmarks per bucket after capture.
perf-bot: perf/regression alert: 1804009876 - LlamaX short-seq p99 +18% (detected 2026-03-16T14:12Z)
maria: Also observed nuance with KV cache eviction: when capture happened the KV cache shape hinting changed slightly and cache reuse across batches dropped for beam=1 short decode, adding ~0.5-1ms variance per request. Not the main p99 culprit but contributing noise.
kevin: Do we have a reliable repro harness? Can we run a sweep: (1) compile on/off, (2) autotune enabled/disabled, (3) capture warmup with short traces? I'll run overnight.
maria: I've pushed a small harness to /perf/runs/llamax/shape_tuning_v4, includes a minimal script:
```
# run on single card
python perf_run.py --model llamaX --buckets 1,32,64,128 --compile={on,off} --autotune={on,off}
```
anna: One more thought: the kernel scorer is currently weighted by throughput only. For short tails we should add a latency-tail penalty term. If the score = alpha*throughput - beta*mem + gamma*tail_latency we can nudge picks.
oliver: Agreed. We also need to ensure kernel variants disabled by capture aren't silently removed from the autotuner candidate set. Capture should emit a "compatibility mask" instead of collapsing variants.
kevin: I'll prototype: (a) modify scorer to include p95/p99 heuristic, (b) run candidate microbenchmarks after capture to validate choices, (c) add seqlen-based compile gating. If overnight runs look good I'll put a canary tomorrow.
maria: Thanks. One more micro-obs: when we force int8 kernels under compile path, we saw slightly higher variance vs f32 on short seq — quantization break-even wins at long sequences. So autotuner needs architecture + seqlen + quantization-aware objectives.
perf-bot: note: added issue INF-1297 "autotuner/compile short-seq regression"
build-bot: CI job perf/llamax/shape_tuning_v4 queued (expected run time ~3h) :gear:
kevin: OK will follow up with results. If anyone has quick ideas to add to the harness (e.g., synthetic prefixes that exercise KV reuse), drop them here.
anna: I'll add a synthetic prefix generator and a pre-capture warmup that runs 50 short-prefixes randomly sampled.
maria: Awesome — let's aim to roll the scorer + gating to canary and monitor p99 for short-seq across the next 48h. :rocket:
